title: Sixteen Years and One Wet Coat
subtitle: 服务行业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 服务行业（社会服务与人际沟通·服务行业与职业）
meta: 主题语境：服务行业（社会服务与人际沟通·服务行业与职业）　|　核心词汇：customer　|　正文 346 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 customer 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 my father ① served a customer that no assistant in the shop would have waited on, and he said the serving was the whole of the trade. The ② customer, meaning the person and not the account, came sixteen years and stayed unnamed in the ledger; a customer, he said, is the only thing in a shop that is judged by how long he is left waiting.

Every ③ customer in that shop had the same wet coat against the counter, and the ④ customer at the end, meaning the one who came on Saturdays and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever remembered twice. A customer, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to serve; my father said the serving is the part that fills sixteen years.

The accountant meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the customer was the whole of the account, meaning the name in the book and not the person. The ⑥ customer, meaning the name in the book and not any of that, is the only thing in an account that everybody numbers and nobody meets; customer, he said, is either somebody you serve or the only word that means both a person and a name. He said the name is the part they remember.

By 1967 the ⑦ customer had become a line in a monthly report, and the report had become an argument about the wet coat. The ⑧ customer of the whole thing, my father wrote in November, was one shop and sixteen years of serving; customer, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to serve. She said the serving was never mentioned.

The ⑨ customer I remember is the one at the end, who last came in 1979 and is still described as the quietest in the town. A ⑩ customer, my mother said in 1981, is the only thing that improves by being served; every customer, she said, is a name that has agreed to look like a person. She said the name was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 顾客；主顾（指进店买东西的那个人）
B. n. 顾客（指那个人本身，与那个账户相对）
C. 固定搭配：serve a customer 接待（服务）一位顾客
D. n. 顾客（指每周六来的那一位）
E. n. 顾客；客源（抽象总称，指一家店的全部客情）
F. n. 客户（指报告里写到、被编号的那一个）
G. n. 客户（指账簿上那个户名）
H. n. 客户（抽象总称，指被编号却无人见面的名字）

items.q: served a customer that no assistant in the shop would have waited on
The customer, meaning the person and not the account
the customer was the whole of the account

answers.why: serve a customer 意为“接待（服务）一位顾客”，1958 年父亲接待了一位店里没有一位店员肯去招呼的顾客。
customer 意为“顾客”，指那个人本身而不是那个账户，他来了十六年而在账簿上始终没有名字。
customer 意为“顾客”，指那家店里每一位顾客，每一位都把同一件湿外套搁在柜台上。
customer 意为“顾客”，指每周六来的那一位，是唯一有人记起过两次的。
customer 意为“客户”，指账簿上那个户名，会计说这个客户就是那个账户的全部。
customer 意为“客户”，指被编号却无人见面的名字而不是别的，是一个账户里人人都编号、却无人见过的东西。
customer 意为“客户”，指报告里写到、被编号的那一个，到 1967 年这位客户成了月报里的一行。
customer 意为“顾客、客源”，父亲十一月写道，整件事的客源是一家店和十六年的接待。
customer 意为“顾客”，我记得的是末尾那一位，1979 年最后一次进店，至今仍被说成镇上最安静的。
customer 为抽象总称，母亲 1981 年说，一位顾客是唯一会因为被好好接待而变得更好的存在。
